To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IGF binding protein 6 is expressed in the adult nervous system in a manner that is tightly linked to the coordination of sensori-motor function.
the expression of BP6 in the nervous system is primarily associated with the hindbrain and peripheral ganglia and that these structures are associated with sensorimotor coordination.

BP6 is highly expressed in the trigeminal ganglion during embryonic development, is highly expressed in hindbrain and spinal cord neurons and dorsal root ganglion in the adult, and is highly expressed in cerebellum neurons in the postnatal and adult animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression profile of IGF binding protein 6 in the developing and mature nervous system.
the expression of the IGF system in the nervous system.
the anatomical distribution and cellular localization of BP6 mRNA in the developing and mature nervous system of the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BP6 is expressed in the CNS in a pattern consistent with its role in the modulation of IGF-II action in the adult nervous system.
BP6 expression is restricted to the hindbrain, cerebellum, cranial and spinal ganglia, with the highest expression in cranial ganglia and spinal cord.
BP6 expression is restricted to sensory nuclei in the adult nervous system, which are associated with sensorimotor integration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BP6 mRNA is expressed at high levels in the embryonic and adult nervous systems and is primarily associated with sensory ganglia and the hindbrain.
the IGF system in the nervous system has a unique role for IGF-II and that the BP6/ IGF-II complex is a critical component of this system.
BP6 mRNA is highly expressed in nuclei that are associated with the control of motor function and is expressed in the adult CNS in the same regions where IGF-II is highly expressed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BP6 has the potential to play a significant role in modulating the function of IGF-II in the nervous system.
BP6 is expressed in a unique pattern in the adult CNS that suggests it has an important role in the modulation of IGF-II actions in these systems.
the IGF binding proteins have distinct and unique roles in the nervous system.
